result.title: Reward Integrity in Adversarial Reinforcement Learning for LLM Guardrail Red-Teaming
result.comment: Received the Best Paper Award at the Reinforcement Learning for LLM Agents Workshop at ACM International Conference for AI in Finance 2026 in Milan
result.summary: We study reward fidelity in an adversarial reinforcement-learning loop for red-teaming financial-services language-model guardrails. Apparent wins can arise when an attack omits prescribed personally identifiable information (PII), or when a reward judge credits a response that did not break the targeted policy. On attacker-generated and public benchmark examples, TypeSafe Jev checks whether the prescribed PII is present. For outcome scoring, we compare the decision models TypeSafe Jev, Laya (pretrained and post-trained), and pretrained CLM-8B with logged Opus 4.8 judgements from a replay corpus. Post-training markedly improves Laya's agreement with the judge. A separate author-reviewed off-target set establishes that Opus can award false wins. The findings motivate specialised decision-model judges for checking prescribed PII in attack inputs and scoring target responses against the intended policy.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究金融领域 LLM 护栏红队测试中对抗强化学习的奖励可靠性，指出攻击未包含规定 PII 或奖励裁判误判时会产生虚假成功，并比较多种决策模型与人工/裁判判断的一致性，主张引入专用裁判模型。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「奖励裁判虚高、虚假胜利需专门核验」的思路可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中的贡献分配与监督信号可靠性，例如判断推理过程是否真正获得对应证据的信用；但属纯文本安全应用，与视觉状态无直接联系。
